key_insight: TEON generalizes Muon's layer-wise matrix orthonormalization by treating network gradients as a structured higher-order tensor and performing tensorized orthonormalization, yielding stronger theoretical convergence and more globally coherent pre-training updates.
problem_solved: Layer-wise Muon only orthogonalizes gradients per-layer (matrix-level), which misses cross-layer / multi-mode correlations in gradients and limits convergence and stability for very large models; TEON addresses this by capturing and regularizing the tensor structure of gradients.
method: Model gradients (or momenta) as a higher-order tensor that spans modes such as layers, parameter axes, heads/positions, etc.

Perform orthonormalization across tensor modes (tensorized orthonormalization) instead of independently per-layer, preserving multi-mode structure and reducing redundant directions across the network.

Provide a theoretical convergence improvement over layer-wise Muon and a practical, computationally efficient implementation (e.g., via mode-wise transforms / low-rank updates) suitable for LLM pre-training.
impact: TEON improves optimization stability and convergence for large-scale model pre-training by enforcing globally consistent, multi-mode orthogonality in gradient space—leading to faster, more reliable training and better utilization of compute for LLMs.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: layer-wise (matrix) orthonormalization vs TEON's tensorized orthonormalization (showing a 3D tensor with orthonormalization across modes).
Flowchart of the TEON update: gradient tensor → mode-wise orthonormalization → orthogonalized update → parameter step.
Convergence plot: training/validation loss or steps-to-convergence comparing Muon, TEON, and a baseline optimizer.
Icon set: tensor/mode icon, convergence/clock icon, stability/shield icon to quickly convey benefits.
paper_title: TEON: Tensorized Orthonormalization Beyond Layer-Wise Muon for Large Language Model Pre-Training
paper_authors: Ruijie Zhang, Yequan Zhao, Ziyue Liu, Zhengyang Wang, Dongyang Li
